items.body: Find the vertex of the parabola $y=(x-3)^2+4$.
items.solution: In the form $y=(x-h)^2+k$ the vertex is $(h,k)$. Here $h=3$ and $k=4$, so the vertex is $(3,4)$. Check: at $x=3$ the squared term is $0$, which is as small as it can get, and $y=4$.

items.body: A discrete random variable $X$ takes the values $1,2,3$ with $P(X=k)=\dfrac{c}{2^k}$. Find $P(X\ge 2)$.
items.solution: The probabilities must total $1$: $$c\left(\tfrac12+\tfrac14+\tfrac18\right)=c\cdot\tfrac78=1,$$ so $c=\tfrac87$. Then $$P(X\ge 2)=c\left(\tfrac14+\tfrac18\right)=\tfrac87\cdot\tfrac38=\tfrac37.$$

errors.C: forgot to find $c$ and added $\tfrac14+\tfrac18$ raw
errors.D: used $c=\tfrac87$ but summed all three probabilities instead of the last two

items.solution: Raise the power by one and divide by the new power: $$\int 6x^2\,dx=\frac{6x^{3}}{3}+C=2x^3+C.$$ Check by differentiating: $\frac{d}{dx}(2x^3)=6x^2$.

items.solution: Integrate first: $F(x)=x^3-2x^2+x+C$. Use the given value to pin $C$: $$F(1)=1-2+1+C=C=5.$$ So $F(x)=x^3-2x^2+x+5$ and $$F(2)=8-8+2+5=7.$$

items.body: The graph of $y=x^2$ is translated $3$ units in the positive $x$-direction. What is the equation of the new graph?
items.solution: A horizontal translation of $a$ to the right replaces $x$ by $x-a$, so $y=x^2$ becomes $y=(x-3)^2$. Check where the vertex went: it was at $x=0$, and $(x-3)^2$ is zero at $x=3$ — three units right, as required.

items.body: $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive with $P(A)=\tfrac25$ and $P(B)=\tfrac12$. Find $P(A\cup B)$.
items.solution: Mutually exclusive means $P(A\cap B)=0$, so the addition rule loses its last term: $$P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)=\tfrac25+\tfrac12=\tfrac{9}{10}.$$

items.body: $P(A)=\tfrac35$, $P(B)=\tfrac12$ and $P(A\cup B)=\tfrac45$. Find the probability that exactly one of $A$ and $B$ occurs.
items.solution: First recover the intersection from the addition rule: $$P(A\cap B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cup B)=\tfrac35+\tfrac12-\tfrac45=\tfrac{3}{10}.$$ ''Exactly one'' is the union with the overlap removed: $$P(A\cup B)-P(A\cap B)=\tfrac45-\tfrac{3}{10}=\tfrac12.$$

items.body: $X$ takes the value $0$ or $1$, each with probability $\tfrac12$. Find $\operatorname{Var}(X)$.
items.solution: $E(X)=0\cdot\tfrac12+1\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac12$ and $E(X^2)=0\cdot\tfrac12+1\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac12$, so $$\operatorname{Var}(X)=E(X^2)-\bigl(E(X)\bigr)^2=\tfrac12-\tfrac14=\tfrac14.$$

items.body: A line passes through $(2,-1)$ and is perpendicular to $3x-4y=8$. Find its equation.
items.solution: Rearrange the given line to $y=\tfrac34x-2$, so its gradient is $\tfrac34$. A perpendicular line has gradient $-\tfrac43$, since $\tfrac34\cdot\left(-\tfrac43\right)=-1$. Through $(2,-1)$: $$y+1=-\tfrac43(x-2)\ \Longrightarrow\ 3y+3=-4x+8\ \Longrightarrow\ 4x+3y=5.$$ Every option passes through $(2,-1)$, so the point alone cannot decide it — only the gradient can.

errors.D: swapped the coefficients without negating, giving gradient $-\tfrac34$

items.body: A bag holds $5$ red and $3$ blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that at least one is red.
items.solution: ''At least one red'' is easier through its complement, ''both blue'': $$P(\text{both blue})=\frac38\cdot\frac27=\frac{3}{28}.$$ Therefore $$P(\text{at least one red})=1-\frac{3}{28}=\frac{25}{28}.$$

items.body: Write $0.4\overline{27}$ (that is, $0.4272727\ldots$) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.solution: Let $x=0.4272727\ldots$. Shift past the non-repeating digit and past one full period: $$10x=4.272727\ldots,\qquad 1000x=427.272727\ldots$$ Subtract: $990x=423$, so $$x=\frac{423}{990}=\frac{47}{110}.$$

errors.B: used $999$, which is the denominator only when ALL digits repeat
errors.C: used $427$ on top, forgetting to subtract the $4$ from the shifted copy
errors.D: used $99$, ignoring the non-repeating digit $4$

items.body: Find the sum of all multiples of $7$ between $100$ and $300$.
items.solution: The first multiple of $7$ above $100$ is $105=7(15)$ and the last below $300$ is $294=7(42)$, so there are $42-15+1=28$ terms. Then $$S=\frac{n(a+l)}{2}=\frac{28(105+294)}{2}=14\times 399=5586.$$

errors.B: used $27$ terms — the classic off-by-one from $42-15$
errors.C: included $301$ as a term
errors.D: forgot to halve, or halved twice

items.body: Simplify $\dfrac{\left(x^{3}y^{-2}\right)^{2}}{x^{-1}y^{3}}$.
items.solution: Apply the power to each factor first: $(x^3y^{-2})^2=x^6y^{-4}$. Then subtract the denominator's exponents: $$x^{6-(-1)}y^{-4-3}=x^{7}y^{-7}=\frac{x^{7}}{y^{7}}.$$

errors.B: treated $y^{-7}$ as $y^{7}$
errors.C: subtracted the $x$ exponents as $6-1$ instead of $6-(-1)$
errors.D: subtracted only the $3$ from the $y$ exponent, forgetting the $-4$

items.body: Evaluate $\log_2 8$.
items.solution: $\log_2 8$ asks: to what power must $2$ be raised to give $8$? Since $2^3=8$, the answer is $3$.

errors.B: answered $\log_2 16$
errors.C: gave the base rather than the exponent
errors.D: inverted the answer

items.body: If $\log_a 8=\tfrac32$, find $a$.
items.solution: Rewrite in exponential form: $a^{3/2}=8$. Raise both sides to the power $\tfrac23$: $$a=8^{2/3}=\left(\sqrt[3]{8}\right)^{2}=2^{2}=4.$$

errors.B: gave $\sqrt[3]{8}$ without squaring it
errors.C: multiplied $8$ by $2$ instead of raising to the power $\tfrac23$
errors.D: computed $8\times\tfrac32$

items.body: Solve $\log_3 x=2$.
items.solution: Convert to exponential form: $x=3^2=9$.

errors.B: multiplied the base by the exponent
errors.C: computed $3^2-1$
errors.D: divided the base by the exponent

items.body: Solve $\log x+\log(x-3)=1$ (logarithms base $10$).
items.solution: Combine the logarithms: $\log\bigl(x(x-3)\bigr)=1$, so $x(x-3)=10$ and $$x^2-3x-10=0\ \Longrightarrow\ (x-5)(x+2)=0.$$ Now check the domain: a logarithm needs a positive argument. $x=-2$ makes $\log x$ undefined, so it is rejected. Only $x=5$ survives.

errors.B: solved the quadratic but never checked that both logarithms are defined
errors.C: kept the rejected root and discarded the valid one
errors.D: set $x-3=10$, applying the $1$ to only one logarithm

items.body: Solve $\log_2(x-1)<3$.
items.solution: The logarithm is only defined when $x-1>0$, so $x>1$ from the start. Since base $2$ is greater than $1$, the function increases and the inequality keeps its direction: $$x-1<2^3=8\ \Longrightarrow\ x<9.$$ Combining, $1<x<9$.

errors.B: solved the inequality but ignored the domain restriction $x>1$
errors.C: reversed the inequality, which only happens for a base below $1$
errors.D: forgot to add the $1$ back after solving for $x-1$

items.body: Evaluate $27^{-2/3}$.
items.solution: The denominator of the exponent is the root and the numerator is the power; the minus sign inverts: $$27^{-2/3}=\frac{1}{\left(\sqrt[3]{27}\right)^{2}}=\frac{1}{3^{2}}=\frac19.$$

errors.B: ignored the minus sign
errors.C: made the result negative instead of taking a reciprocal
errors.D: squared $27$ before taking the cube root, then inverted
